hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to distinct, high-contrast dark objects or silhouettes—typically black or deep charcoal—positioned centrally against a lighter, monochromatic background of medium to light grey. The activating feature often takes the form of a compact, isolated subject such as a spider, insect, dark animal head, liquid droplet, vehicle silhouette, or instrument part, which stands out sharply due to its tonal density relative to the featureless or textured grey surroundings. The neuron remains invariant to the object's specific identity, texture (whether glossy, metallic, or furred), and orientation, as long as the polarity of a dark figure against a lighter, desaturated field is maintained. The focal dark feature typically occupies approximately 15–40% of the image area and is centrally positioned or slightly offset within the frame.
